name: Mimic 3
description: Mycroft AI's VITS-based neural TTS server (MycroftAI/mimic3) with a web UI, REST API, and MaryTTS-compatible endpoints on port 59125. Quart/Hypercorn, no authentication. Project is abandoned (Mycroft AI shut down). Server-rendered index makes it cleanly Shodan http.html-visible.
auth_notes: No authentication. mimic3-server (the mimic3_http module) is a Quart app behind Hypercorn; all routes (api/tts, api/voices, /openapi, MaryTTS-compat /process, /voices, /version) are public. Default launch is '--host localhost --port 59125', but the official Docker image binds 0.0.0.0:59125. No API key, token, or basic auth. Designed as a local appliance for the Mycroft Mark II, with no access controls; the project is abandoned so no auth will ever be added.

shodan_dorks.query: port:59125 http.html:"Mimic 3 text to speech server"
shodan_dorks.rationale: The server-rendered Bootstrap index contains 'Mimic 3 text to speech server' verbatim in the body; direct high-signal match on the canonical MaryTTS-compatible port.
The index credits Mycroft and the Mark II ('Mycroft's newest text to speech system developed for the Mark II'); the Mimic 3 + Mycroft co-occurrence in the body is nearly unique across any port.
Conjunctive: the Mimic 3 heading plus the api/tts endpoint referenced in the UI on port 59125 isolates it from other Quart/Hypercorn TTS servers and from a raw MaryTTS server on the same port.
The VITS parameter lengthScale (with noiseScale/noiseW) is exposed in the Mimic 3 UI form; its presence pins the VITS-based Mimic 3 specifically for build/version scoping via /version.

response_body_contains: does not store the text you send

known_vulns: No authentication - unauthenticated synthesis via api/tts and voice enumeration via api/voices
Abandoned (Mycroft AI shut down) - README warns it 'is no longer maintained and may not work'; no patches ever
VITS noise/length-scale parameters (noiseScale, noiseW, lengthScale) exposed for unauthenticated compute abuse and DoS
SSML processor is an unaudited input surface; ssml=true toggles a broader parser path
/openapi/ Swagger UI publicly documents the whole API unauthenticated
MaryTTS-compatible /process endpoint makes it a drop-in Home Assistant TTS backend that may be left internet-exposed
risk_notes: Vectors on an exposed instance: (1) Unauthenticated synthesis / GPU-or-CPU compute theft via api/tts; the VITS controls (noiseScale, noiseW, lengthScale) let an attacker drive heavy inference at operator cost with no rate limit; (2) Voice enumeration via api/voices; (3) SSML parser surface via the ssml=true path; (4) Abandonment - Mycroft AI is defunct and the README explicitly warns the project is unmaintained, so any finding is permanent with no upstream fix. Mimic 3 is cleanly Shodan http.html-visible: the server-rendered Bootstrap index carries 'Mimic 3', 'Mimic 3 text to speech server', the Mycroft/Mark II credit, the 'does not store the text you send' privacy line, and author credit 'Michael Hansen' in the body, so a title or body dork harvests it directly. Server header is 'hypercorn-h11', identical to OpenTTS - disambiguate by port (59125 vs 5500) and the Mimic 3 body strings. The MaryTTS-compatible /process route means exposed Home Assistant setups are a common source of wild instances.
deployment_notes: Quart app behind Hypercorn (logs show 'INFO:hypercorn.error' and 'Running on http://0.0.0.0:59125'). Default CLI bind is localhost:59125, but the official Docker image mycroftai/mimic3 (with a Dockerfile.gpu variant for CUDA) binds 0.0.0.0:59125 via 'docker run -p 59125:59125 mycroftai/mimic3'. Port 59125 is the MaryTTS-compatible port, chosen so Mimic 3 drops into MaryTTS-expecting clients (notably Home Assistant). Server header is 'hypercorn-h11'. Because the index is server-rendered the Mimic 3 identity is in http.html; /version gives the build and /openapi/ documents the API. ~1.3k stars, AGPLv3; not formally git-archived but dead following Mycroft AI's shutdown. Shares the Quart/Hypercorn stack with OpenTTS - distinguish on port and the Mimic 3 body strings.
